statement: ISO treatment requires that no disposition of the share occur within 2 years from the grant of the option nor within 1 year after the transfer of the share to the individual (26 U.S.C. § 422(a)(1)). On a disqualifying disposition, the increase in income attributable to the exercise (the exercise-date spread) is treated as income of the taxable year of the disposition (§ 421(b)), and where the disposition is a sale at a loss to which § 422(c)(2) applies, the includible amount cannot exceed the excess of the amount realized over the adjusted basis of the share; § 421(b) also provides no employer withholding is required on that income.
caveat: § 422(c)(2) applies only to dispositions on which a loss, if sustained, would be recognized (e.g. not wash sales or related-party sales), and day counting at the exact anniversary boundary is a legal determination. A disposition after a qualifying holding period yields capital gain or loss measured against the exercise price for regular tax; AMT basis differs (rule us-fed.iso-amt-adjustment).
